title: Android was built for cameras.
description:
Android was built for cameras. Andy Rubin pitched investors in 2004 a camera platform with a cloud portion for storing images online.

Founded Android Inc. in Palo Alto in October 2003.

Camera growth was slowing. Rubin said handsets were the bigger opportunity, and a free operating system could undercut rivals.

The same platform became Android for cellphones. 'The exact same platform, the exact same operating system we built for cameras', said in Tokyo on 16 April 2013.

The founders joined Google with it. Rubin, Rich Miner, Nick Sears and Chris White all moved across.

Sold as the T-Mobile G1, the first commercial Android phone, announced 23 September 2008.

Sources:
- https://www.pcworld.com/article/451350/android-founder-we-aimed-to-make-a-camera-os.html - Andy Rubin, Japan New Economy Summit, Tokyo, 16 April 2013: 'The exact same platform, the exact same operating system we built for cameras, that became Android for cellphones'; camera market growth was slowing; handsets were the bigger opportunity and a free OS could undercut rivals.
- https://www.dpreview.com/articles/0013837043/android-was-originally-designed-for-cameras/ - corroborated that the 2004 investor pitch was 'a camera platform with a cloud portion for storing images online', and that the team repurposed it as a handset OS as camera growth slowed.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) - founding in October 2003 in Palo Alto by Andy Rubin and Chris White, the original FotoFrame camera OS project, the April 2004 pivot to phones, Google's 2005 acquisition, and the HTC Dream announced 23 September 2008 as the first commercial Android phone.
